answer: Device-bound identity sessions stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each agent registers one hardware key, so one device equals one identity. Second, every job is signed by that device, giving a signal a copy cannot fake. Third, a device switch starts a thirty day cooldown with peer checks. Fourth, sharing burns registration for a year and forfeits the bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 devices at $60 each, $60,000, plus $12,000 in fees, lost on detection. Trust grows like an orchard, and a bridge holds only with planks, like a stall whose owner must appear daily to keep customers.
